title: Isolated Server Foundation Slice
summary: P0 design and bounded P1 implementation: PostgreSQL-backed project registry, explicit migrations, token authorization and transactional management audit.
delivery: Separate server/CMakeLists.txt and server/VERSION. Server links native Core without adding HTTP/PostgreSQL dependencies to Core. Use the accepted configuration and complete required policies from docs/machine/shin-companion-protocols-v1.json, including its template and check-config gate. Source-host/workspace binding and an independently reviewed database.server_id pin remain required. Stable delivery is independently owned by the sibling checkout; the historical foundation version below is not its current version.
scope: separate process liveness and database readiness

http.scope: Bounded synchronous workers for short management requests. This choice is not yet validated for long-lived MCP or event subscriptions.

dependencies.libpq: System client >=13, isolated native development uses 18.6.
dependencies.postgresqlTestServer: 18.6 in a dedicated Docker Compose project and volume.
dependencies.json: Existing nlohmann dependency; bounded strict parse with duplicate-key rejection.
dependencies.crypto: OpenSSL EVP SHA256 and constant-time digest comparison; no custom cryptographic primitive.

api.envelope: shin.server-response.v1 with explicit server version, development stability, ok, and exactly result or error.
api.GET /health/ready: Authenticated database/schema readiness; not project or retrieval readiness.
api.POST /api/v1/projects: Administrator, exact JSON fields id/display_name, required Idempotency-Key. Logical registration has no filesystem prerequisite or automatic adoption. Separate workspace endpoints bind local roots; see shin-server-workspaces-v1.
api.GET /api/v1/projects: Project-scoped keyset page, after identifier and limit 1..100.
api.GET /api/v1/projects/{id}: One permitted project; absent and unauthorized identifiers both return 404.
api.GET /api/v1/audit: Project-scoped management history, after sequence and limit 1..100.
api.errorPolicy: Do not return driver errors, SQL, tokens, conninfo, input excerpts or filesystem exception text.

authorization.principals: Explicit private configuration contains token SHA256 digests, principal ids and admin/reader roles. Readers have an explicit project id set. No account-management API is claimed.
authorization.credentials: Generate high-entropy tokens externally. Keep plaintext only in private local files; never in source, logs or CLI arguments.
authorization.http: Bind 127.0.0.1 only in this slice. Validate Host and any Origin header. No wildcard CORS or unauthenticated management.
authorization.files: Configuration and conninfo must be bounded, private, owned, regular nonsymlink files. Root registration resolves canonical paths under an explicit allowlist and records filesystem identity.

database.name: Expected database identity is explicit and checked; development uses shin_server_dev.
database.runtime: Limited runtime role, no superuser or DDL authority. Migration uses separate credentials through an explicit command.
database.schema: Version/checksum history and expected table/column/key layout are checked on database access. This is schema compatibility validation, not a guarantee against a malicious database administrator or arbitrary equivalent DDL replacement.
database.writeUnit: Project row, management audit event and idempotency result commit together. P3D2 activation commits route head, receipt and audit together; audit_events.activation_route_id plus activation_previous_revision form a nullable paired foreign key to the receipt.
database.retry: Same principal/key/request returns the original project with replayed=true. A changed request under that key conflicts. Logical project ids are unique; source-host/root exclusion belongs to the separate workspace registry.
database.rollback: Failed writes must not leave a project, audit event or idempotency claim behind.
database.availability: An unavailable database blocks database operations, not process liveness. Connections recover without restarting the application.
database.auditCursor: All server audit writers take the same PostgreSQL transaction advisory lock before identity allocation and hold it through commit. This avoids skipping a delayed lower id when paginating by committed audit id. The rule is cooperative across server writers, not a cryptographic audit or protection from an out-of-band DBA writer.
database.performanceBoundary: This first implementation verifies schema and runtime role on every acquired database operation. Round-trip cost and bounded worker concurrency are deliberate correctness-first baseline costs, not optimized warm retrieval.

initialBudgets.workerScope: These are HTTP workers. Opt-in P3A adds one preparation worker and one heartbeat thread during an active preparation; Core generation may use its profile-selected bounded parallelism.
initialBudgets.httpTimeoutMeaning: Socket read/write timeouts, not a universal end-to-end request deadline. The loopback development listener is not internet-hardened or certified for untrusted slow-client load.
initialBudgets.performancePolicy: Record a first warm registry/authorization baseline before later optimization. These resource caps are enforced limits, not unmeasured p95 claims or retrieval performance guarantees.
